Subject: Scoped model-improvement exclusion and response custody

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — Greenfield's team is excited about Redwood’s latency/cost profile. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of specific items that legal will need for the DPA and SOW: 

- A firm commitment that Greenfield’s production interactions will not be used to improve models (no model-training or model-improvement use).
- Clarity on response ownership: our clinicians want written confirmation that generated responses are licensed to Greenfield for their internal product use and regulatory recordkeeping.
- A practical rollback path: in the event we need to reverse any model variant changes or remove adaptive updates tied to Greenfield traffic, what is your operational remediation timeline and scope?

Can you send an initial DPA sketch or redline we can pass to counsel? Also—do you have any operational proof (flow diagram or matrix) showing which subprocessors touch inference payloads and what onshore/eu routing options exist?

Would you be available for a short call Thursday to run through these items with our GC (Laura)?

Appreciate it,
Maya

Maya Singh

Greenfield Health

Subject: Re: Scoped model-improvement exclusion and response custody

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely walk through these items. High-level answers first, then I attached a draft DPA sketch and a scoped "Model Improvement & Subprocessor Matrix" (see attachments) that maps which components see tenant data.

- No-model-improvement commitment: We can offer a contractual prohibition on using Greenfield production interactions for model training or model improvement (we typically use the phrase "no model improvement from customer interactions" in the DPA). Operationally we implement this via separate ingest pipelines and a tenant-level flag that prevents retention to any training feeds.

- Response/license: We propose language that grants Greenfield an irrevocable, transferable license to generated outputs for their business purposes and regulatory retention. We do not claim ownership of customer prompts or outputs beyond what’s necessary to operate the service.

- Rollback/remediation path: Attached matrix includes an "Operational Rollback" section. In short: for hosted model variant rollbacks affecting Greenfield, we can initiate a rollback within 24 hours and complete state reconciliation (KV cache purge, prefix cache resets) within 72 hours for in-flight sessions. If a rollback requires re-routing to a previous model binary, that can be staged within a 5 business-day window subject to scheduled maintenance windows and validation. We include an option for a temporary throttled circuit-breaker to isolate traffic while we validate the rollback.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please review the attached DPA sketch and matrix and flag any must-have redlines.
2) Kimberly (cc'd) will review the DPA language for compliance/legal risk.
3) If Greenfield wants an auditable proof-of-implementation, we can prepare an operations runbook excerpt and an evidence pack for SOC/SFTP export that shows the tenant routing and retention flags.

Would Thursday 10:00 AM PT work for a 30-minute call?

Best,

--
Mina Haddad
Customer Solutions (Privacy & Compliance lead)
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Maya / team — adding legal context and a couple of drafting notes for the DPA sketch Mina shared. Quoting Mina's points below for clarity.

> - No-model-improvement commitment: We can offer a contractual prohibition on using Greenfield production interactions for model training or model improvement...

Drafting notes: 
- We recommend the customer-facing clause read: "Provider will not use Customer Data for model training, fine-tuning, or model improvement, except as explicitly agreed in writing." Avoid overly broad language that inadvertently prohibits normal performance monitoring and telemetry; we propose a carveout limited to operational telemetry (latency metrics, error rates) that are aggregated and not tenant-identifiable.
- For "response license" we propose dual tracks: (a) a primary clause granting Greenfield rights to use and retain generated responses for internal and regulatory use, and (b) an optional SOW addendum for customers who want export/transfer rights for product redistribution.
- Rollback SLAs: Operational rollback timelines are fine, but legal wants to bound liability. We'll add a Service Level and a maximum window (e.g., we will use reasonable commercial efforts to execute rollback within 5 business days, with the 24/72 windows described as our target operational commitment).

One more ask from counsel: can you include the subprocessor contract names and whether retention occurs in encrypted form with onshore KMS options? If any subprocessor is a managed inference partner (third-party runtime), flag that explicitly — it often triggers a security review and additional assurances.

I can prepare a redline of the DPA sketch by EOD Wednesday.

-Kim

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Hi Maya — ops follow-up and a couple of implementation clarifications before the call: 

- Subprocessors & encryption: All inference traffic is TLS in transit; persisted telemetry or logs are encrypted at rest. For customers requiring onshore key control we can enable a dedicated KMS option (bring-your-own-key or our onshore KMS) for the tenant metadata store. The attached matrix shows which subprocessors touch non-ephemeral storage.
- Tenant isolation and flags: We operate a tenant-scoped retention flag that prevents writes to model improvement feeds. We will provide an ops-runbook excerpt on the call showing the flag lifecycle (enable, audit, revoke).
- Rollback verification: Our validation checklist includes KV cache invalidation, running canary traffic against the previous model, and sampling regression tests. For customers in regulated workflows we offer a verification window where we produce a verification report (timestamped) confirming the rollback steps performed. For auditability we can produce cryptographic hashes of model binaries and acceptance logs if needed.

I'll join the Thursday call and bring the ops runbook excerpt. Confirming 10:00 AM PT Thursday — I've created a calendar invite.

Thanks,
David
